label: Camels

sources.text: Camelidae (Gray, 1821), a family in the suborder Tylopoda of the order Artiodactyla; the only living family in that suborder, as given in the article.

names.text: 'Camels' is the item's given label. The article's own name is the family name Camelidae, with no separate common name for the family taken from it.

about.text: The family of camels and llamas. Its milk-giving members are the dromedary and the Bactrian camel, which the article lists as the two camel species of the genus Camelus.

links.name: FAOSTAT: Crops and livestock products (QCL), world, 2023

sources.text: The family's living species and genera are from the Wikipedia article as fetched (camels in tribe Camelini, genus Camelus; llamas and relatives in tribe Lamini, genus Lama). The milk claim is limited to camels: FAOSTAT's 2023 camel figure (4.08 million t, dromedary and Bactrian together) is in research/herd/faostat-2023.json. The llama and alpaca are not milked in the species table here.

gaps: The article was read to character 100000 of 102173; the last 2173 characters were not read. The llamas and alpacas are not claimed to be milked for any figure here. No family-level milk total is given, since the species records carry it.
